title: Canonical session ledger and credit checkpoints for partial uploads & resume semantics
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: We see sporadic duplicate or missing token debits for long-lived sessions that are uploaded in shards or re-tried through proxies. Existing fragment-dedupe logic relies on client-provided IDs and heuristics that break when uploads are reshuffled (CDN/proxy reorder) or when partial uploads are stitched by edge gateways. This causes customer-visible billing skews and requires manual ledger adjustments.

Goal: Introduce a canonical session ledger concept and a lightweight checkpoint/anchor protocol that makes partial-upload, resume, and reassembly idempotent from a metering perspective. The ledger authority will be the single source of truth for credit anchors per session and will support retroactive patching via a reconciliation endpoint. The feature should work across HTTP multipart, websocket chunking, and proxied replays.

Non-goals: Replace existing tokenization/credit math; this work focuses on attribution, checkpointing, and reconciliation only.
background: Incidents: multiple customer tickets in Jan-Feb where billing mismatch correlated with multipart uploads and CDN retries.
Existing protections: fragment dedupe, speculative provisional credits, and session snapshots. These fail when sequence ordering is lost or when attachments are re-chunked by intermediaries.
Constraints: Minimal latency impact for short sessions; ledger operations must be idempotent and retry-safe; storage footprint should be bounded per active session.
design_summary: Introduce a canonical session ledger record (session_ledger) keyed by session_id + tenant and owned by metering-service.
Attach monotonic checkpoints called credit_anchors (anchor_id, stable_offset, cumulative_token_count, checksum) to ledger; anchors are immutable once committed.

Clients/edge gateways submit chunk envelopes containing resume_token and optional chunk_seq. Metering-service maps envelopes to the nearest anchor candidate and accepts only deltas beyond committed anchors.

Reconciliation API (/metering/reconcile) allows the console or an automated backfill job to submit observed final_token_count and a patch request; if the final count exceeds committed anchors, ledger emits a single retro-active credit event.
Use lightweight optimistic locking with anchor sequence numbers and an anti-duplication idempotency key for inbound chunk acknowledgement operations.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical ledger created for sessions with multipart uploads and streaming; new ledger entries observable in the metering admin UI.
No duplicate credits emitted for artificially re-ordered or re-chunked uploads in fuzz tests (simulate CDN/proxy reorder and replay).
Reconciliation endpoint can apply a single retroactive credit per logical finalization; reconciliation log entry appears in audit trail and is reconciled in billing reports.
E2E benchmarks show median 95th-percentile addition of latency for new sessions < 6ms; small overhead on hot paths validated against runtime-1.26.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (design + proto): implement in metering-service a session_ledger table and anchor write/read endpoints. Wire basic idempotency key check. (2w)
Phase 2 (ingest adapters): update streaming proxy adapter and HTTP multipart handler to emit chunk envelopes with resume_token and optional chunk_seq. Add small envelope parser in front-end. (1w)
Phase 3 (reconciliation): build /metering/reconcile API and a backfill worker that can be run on-demand against historical session logs. Add automated tests and CI. (1w)
Phase 4 (rollout): gradual rollout behind feature flag, monitor invoice deltas, and enable reconciliation worker for initial customer cohorts. (1w)
Phase 5 (retrospective): tuning, postmortem, and migration scripts to convert provisional sessions to anchored ledgers. (1w)
Total: ~6 weeks of cross-team work, can be broken into parallel streams.
testing_plan: Property-based tests that simulate arbitrary reorder, duplicate, and partial-chunk reassembly patterns; assert single-credit outcome.
Integration test with console: create long multipart upload through proxy, intentionally reorder frames, finalize session, call reconcile with final token counts, verify ledger and invoice delta.
Load test: synthetic sessions at 10k RPS across many tenants to validate storage and locking strategy; observe tail latencies and contention metrics.
Manual exploratory: run against recent customer incident logs to verify that reconciliation produces expected corrections.
rollout_plan: Canary to 5% of traffic for 72h with automated billing sanity checks.
If metrics stable, expand to 50% then 100% over 1 week.
Run reconciliation backfill for top-10 impacted tenants during canary and verify invoice deltas before full rollout.
migration_steps: Run one-time migration to seed session_ledger for sessions that have clear finalization markers in logs; mark others as provisional.
Provisional sessions continue to use legacy dedupe; reconciliation worker can convert provisional -> anchored when final counts observed.
Add a delay window (48h) for retroactive credits to detect duplicates in backfill.
risks_and_mitigation: Increased contention on ledger writes: mitigate with sharded anchors by tenant and time-window, and use optimistic retries.
Under-attribution during rollout causing lost credits: keep provisional parallel-writing of legacy credits until canary verified, enabling fallback toggle.
Reconciliation abuse (malformed final counts): require signed proofs (checksum of concatenated chunk checksums) and rate-limit reconcile API.
open_questions: What retention window do we want for anchors? (default proposal: 90d active, 365d archived)
Should reconcilations create explicit invoice adjustments or a separate retro credit ledger that billing can ingest?
Do we need tenant-scoped cryptographic resume_token signing to prevent replay attacks across proxies?
